# Redirect to a URL from HTTP request data (Node.js)

`qualor:js/open-redirect` · Issue · Severity: Medium · [CWE-601](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/601.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A01:2025 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A01_2025-Broken_Access_Control/), [A01:2021 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A01_2021-Broken_Access_Control/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
Redirects whose target is decided by HTTP request data: Express's `res.redirect()` and
`res.location()`, Fastify's `reply.redirect()`, Next.js `redirect()`, `permanentRedirect()` and
`NextResponse.redirect()`, `Response.redirect()`, and a `Location` header set by hand. The rule
reports request data that forms the whole target, its scheme or its host, also after an origin
without a trailing `/` (where `@evil.example` names another host) or after a single `/` (where
`//evil.example` does).
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
A link such as `https://shop.example/login?next=https://evil.example` looks like a link to your
site, but after signing in the user lands on another one. Attackers use this for convincing
phishing pages and to carry tokens from a sign-in flow to a host they control.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the `next` parameter is the whole redirect target.

```javascript
const express = require('express');

const app = express();

app.get('/after-login', (req, res) => {
  res.redirect(req.query.next);
});
```

**Compliant:** the parameter only picks one of a few fixed targets.

```javascript
const express = require('express');

const app = express();

const TARGETS = { orders: '/orders', settings: '/settings' };

app.get('/after-login', (req, res) => {
  res.redirect(TARGETS[req.query.next] ?? '/');
});
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Redirect to a path that starts with a fixed segment: `'/users/' + id`.
- Or to a fixed origin followed by `/`, `?` or `#`: `'https://shop.example/' + path`.
- Encode a single path segment with `encodeURIComponent()`.
- Or map the request value to a target through an allow-list (a `const` table of literals).

A target that only "starts with `/`" is not enough: `//evil.example` starts with `/` and is a link
to another host.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Express
- Next.js
- Fastify
- Node.js http

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A check before the call ("starts with `/` but not `//`", a comparison of the parsed host,
  `[...].includes(x) ? x : '/'`) is not recognised: the checked value is still reported.
- Headers count as request data, so a redirect to `'https://' + req.headers.host + req.originalUrl`
  or to the `Referer` is reported.
- A target built in a variable first is taken as safe only when it starts with a recognisable
  fixed origin or path (an upper-case constant, `process.env`, a config object, a `const` literal);
  concatenations of more than six parts are not checked.
- Results of awaited calls on other objects (a database lookup by a request value) are taken for
  stored data, so a helper that returns the request value it is given is missed.
- Next.js Server Actions and page props are not request sources.
- Request handlers are recognised by the name of their second parameter (`res`, `reply`, `ctx`,
  `next`, ...): a handler written as `(request, out)` is not checked.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test files [`rules/js/redirect/open-redirect.js`](../../../rules/js/redirect/open-redirect.js) and [`rules/js/redirect/open-redirect.ts`](../../../rules/js/redirect/open-redirect.ts) hold every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/js/redirect/open-redirect.yml`](../../../rules/js/redirect/open-redirect.yml), added in version 2026.10.1.
